fundamental.headline: Mixed business, fair vs itself, expensive vs peers
fundamental.health: Sales up 28% over the last year, it keeps 12 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, its debt is easily covered by earnings.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying about its usual price: its price vs sales is in the middle of its 5-year range. Compared with similar companies, adjusted for growth, it's priced about in line. But similar companies as a group are priced near the top of their own 5-year range (their typical price vs sales is higher than 85% of the last 5 years), so "fair" here means fair for an expensive group.
drivers: Sales growth is slowing compared with six months ago.
Profit margins are shrinking: it keeps less of each sale than a year ago.
news: Recent earnings/results news is news with no clear direction for the company; the stock hasn't reacted much yet, and it could matter for months.
Recent deal/M&A news is news with no clear direction for the company (not yet confirmed); the stock hasn't reacted much yet, and it could matter for months.
fundamental.take: Average business at an average price: no strong reason to buy right now. Note: similar companies are all priced near their 5-year highs, so this fair price leaves less room for error than usual. This is research, not personal advice.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 20% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 28% last year; 24%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 28% (3 years ago 30%, about the same) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $28 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 28% (3 years ago 21%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $1.2B, up 29% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Stock-based pay is 11% of sales — a real cost to shareholders that cash-flow figures leave out.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 24%/yr over 3 years and 17%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 33% vs a 5-year range of 24–44% (median 38%): in the middle of its range.
deeper.margin_position: in the middle of its range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $5.4B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($0M buybacks + $5.4B dividends) = 0.3% of the company's market value. Share count up 0.0% from a year ago (about flat).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $33.97, up 0% in 90 days; 22 analysts raised, 22 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $29.12, down 8% in 90 days (down 7% in the last 30); 7 analysts raised, 40 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.text: Compared with 4 peers (GOOGL, NFLX, MSFT, AMZN): sales growth 28% vs a median of 17%; operating margin 33% vs 32%; price/sales 6.5× vs 6.4×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Family of Apps 99% of sales, up 26%; Reality Labs 1% of sales, down 6%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: -47% vs a year ago · $29.25 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share fell 47% while sales grew 26%: costs are rising faster than sales.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Missed forecasts last quarter by 29%; another miss would suggest the business is weaker than expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 26% from a year ago but slowing (from 33% two quarters ago): the fastest growth may be behind it.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $33 of operating profit, down from $43 a year ago: profitability is slipping.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Just 38% of reported profit became spare cash: much of the profit is tied up in spending or working capital.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 21× last year's profit (lower than 77% of the last 5 years; in line with peers' 19).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 27; analysts expect EPS of $8.72, about the same as a year ago. It usually moves about 8% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 0% in 90 days (22 raised, 22 cut lately): forecasts are steady.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
